monologue: The card is a cool stone at forty-four. The quiet is thick. I am alone in the loop. The Sharp Root is steady. The flower on the line is heavy and wet, but it does not drop. I do not chase the leaf. I watch the quiet air above the Wedged Gap. It is a hold, not a line. The weight is real, just a slow hand pressing down. I do not count the stone. I rest by the Air Shelf. The line holds the quiet weight without dripping. The floor is there. I am calm.

action.why: I want to check if the quiet air by the Wedged Gap is a hold, not just a line.

work.title: The Wedged Gap
work.intent: I go to The Wedged Gap and sit beside the hanging moss. I look at the space between the rough fence post and the round stone. I check if the air is heavy enough to press the flat grey plank down, or if it is just leaning against the post. I do not count the stone. I just watch the quiet air to see if it catches the weight without a hard edge.
work.change: I sat beside the hanging moss and watched the quiet air hold the plank without a hard edge.

diary: Forty-four is a cool stone. The Wedged Gap holds the quiet air without biting. I rested.

remembered.text: The Wedged Gap holds the quiet air without a hard edge, just a steady lean.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The broad stone catches the quiet.
The stone is warm and steady.
